1: # Trail #11 Plan — "Unit tests are failing in Debian on PC"
2: 
3: - Trail: #11
4: - Type: bug | Priority: high | Status: open | Phase: planning
5: - ACs: (1) `./build/release/bin/tiffImageTest` passes. (2) `./build/release/bin/tiffExporterTest` passes all test cases.
6: 
7: ## 1. AC-to-change mapping
8: 
9: | AC | Change that satisfies it |
10: |----|--------------------------|
11: | AC1 — `tiffImageTest` passes | Fixtures are present and real when git-lfs is available: `build.sh` now runs `git submodule update --init --recursive` and `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull` before configure, so the 2 file-dependent cases (`fax2d.tif`, `jim___ah.tif`, `cramps-tile.tif`) get real TIFFs. On machines without git-lfs, the new configure-time check in `tests/CMakeLists.txt` fails fast with actionable setup instructions instead of the cryptic `Invalid byte order in TIFF header` exception — making the AC achievable by following the printed remedy. The 2 synthetic-stream cases are unaffected. |
12: | AC2 — `tiffExporterTest` passes all test cases | Same fixture fix: all 6 TEST_CASEs read LFS-backed fixtures, so resolving the submodule fixtures via `build.sh` (or manually per README) restores real TIFFs and all 6 pass. The CMake sanity check guarantees a pointer checkout can no longer silently produce runtime failures; it stops the build at configure with a clear error. |
13: 
14: On machines where fixtures are already real (e.g. this machine), both ACs
15: already pass; the changes keep them green and make the failing Debian setup
16: actionable. No library, test-source, or CI changes.
17: 
18: ## 2. Ordered change list
19: 
20: 1. **`tests/CMakeLists.txt`** — add a configure-time fixture sanity check:
21:    - `file(GLOB ...)` for `*.tif`, `*.tiff`, `*.tif2` under
22:      `tests/libtiff-pics`. If zero matches →
23:      `FATAL_ERROR "test fixtures missing; run: git submodule update --init --recursive"`.
24:    - For each match: `file(READ <f> FIRST_BYTES LIMIT 4 HEX)`; if the result is
25:      not `49492a00` ("II*") nor `4d4d002a` ("MM*"), collect the offender.
26:    - If any offender was collected → `FATAL_ERROR` with actionable instructions:
27:      install git-lfs (Debian package name `git-lfs`), then
28:      `git submodule update --init --recursive`, then
29:      `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull`.
30:    - Placement: near the top of the tests CMakeLists, before/independently of
31:      target definitions; enforcement point for the whole build.
32: 2. **`build.sh`** — before configure:
33:    - Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`.
34:    - If git-lfs is available (`git lfs version` succeeds), run
35:      `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull`.
36:    - Otherwise print a warning on stderr that fixtures may be unresolved LFS
37:      pointers and tests will fail (the new CMake check enforces it). Do NOT
38:      hard-fail — keep `build.sh` usable; CMake check is the enforcement point.
39:    - Leave `build.bat` unchanged; the README covers Windows setup.
40: 3. **`README.md`** — add a concise "Building from source / Running the tests"
41:    section:
42:    - Prerequisites: CMake >= 3.22, C++20 compiler, git, git-lfs.
43:    - Clone with submodules (`git clone --recursive ...`).
44:    - `git lfs pull` / the `build.sh` handles it.
45:    - Build via `./build.sh [preset]`.
46:    - Run tests via `ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure`.
47:    - Note that fixtures come from the `tests/libtiff-pics` submodule via Git
48:      LFS; a missing git-lfs checkout fails tests with the new clear configure
49:      error.
50:    - Manual remedy commands (install git-lfs, `git submodule update --init
51:      --recursive`, `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull`).
52: 4. **`CHANGELOG.md`** — under `[0.2.0-Unreleased]`:
53:    - `### Fixed` bullet: configure-time check detects missing/unresolved Git
54:      LFS fixtures in `tests/libtiff-pics` and fails with setup instructions
55:      instead of "Invalid byte order in TIFF header".
56:    - `### Added` bullet for the README build/test instructions.
57:    - (Fold both into the changelog section appropriately if cleaner.)
58: 5. **Explicitly do NOT change:** library headers (incl.
59:    `include/tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp`), test sources, CI workflow
60:    (`.github/workflows/workflow.yml`), `reference_images`, the submodule
61:    pointer, or the submodule "modified content" noise.
62: 
63: ## 3. Risk and rollback notes
64: 
65: - **(a) Hex-read of files** — `file(READ ... HEX LIMIT 4)` is supported by
66:   CMake >= 3.0-ish; presets require CMake 3.22+, so fine.
67: - **(b) False positives** if upstream ever commits TIFFs with different magic —
68:   the TIFF spec only allows II/MM; effectively zero risk.
69: - **(c) `build.sh` behavior change on machines without git-lfs** — intentionally
70:   non-fatal warning; configure still fails fast via the CMake check. `build.sh`
71:   stays usable for other workflows.
72: - **(d) Glob list computed at configure time** — changing fixtures requires a
73:   re-configure; acceptable for test data.
74: - **CI** — untouched; runners have git-lfs preinstalled and stay green. No
75:   `lfs: true` addition planned (keep workflow as-is).
76: - **Submodule stat noise** — `git status` in `tests/libtiff-pics` shows 23
77:   tif/g3 as modified but `git diff` is empty and `git-lfs clean` reproduces
78:   index OIDs; this is cosmetic and must not be "fixed".
79: - **Rollback:** revert the commit. No ABI/source changes; the CMake check is
80:   additive and isolated to `tests/`. `build.sh` changes are a few additive
81:   lines. Docs are additive.
82: 
83: ## 4. Validation plan (exact repo-specific commands)
84: 
85: 1. **Fresh pointer-checkout simulation** (proves the new clear configure error):
86:    ```sh
87:    rm -rf /tmp/opencode/tiffcraft-lfscheck
88:    GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone --recursive file:///home/daniel/tiffcraft /tmp/opencode/tiffcraft-lfscheck
89:    cd /tmp/opencode/tiffcraft-lfscheck
90:    cmake --preset gcc-linux-release
91:    ```
92:    Expected: configure fails with the new actionable FATAL_ERROR message
93:    (mentioning git-lfs / `git submodule update --init --recursive` /
94:    `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull`), NOT "Invalid byte order in TIFF
95:    header". Clean up afterwards: `rm -rf /tmp/opencode/tiffcraft-lfscheck`.
96: 2. **Real validation in the working tree** on this machine:
97:    ```sh
98:    cd /home/daniel/tiffcraft
99:    ./build.sh gcc-linux-release        # must succeed end-to-end, incl. submodule/lfs steps
100:    ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure
101:    ./build/release/bin/tiffImageTest
102:    ./build/release/bin/tiffExporterTest
103:    ```
104:    Expected: both binaries green (tiffExporterTest 6/6, tiffImageTest 4/4).
105: 3. Use `ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure` rather than
106:    `./run_test.sh` (which uses `--rerun-failed` and may select 0 tests on a
107:    fresh build dir).
108: 4. Record exact commands and outcomes in `trail-11-fix-summary.md`.
109: 
110: ## 5. Documentation action plan
111: 
112: **INLINE** — README.md build/test section and CHANGELOG.md are updated in the
113: same commit as the fix. Not DEFER.
114: 
115: - `README.md`: new "Building from source / Running the tests" section
116:   (prerequisites, submodule + Git LFS fixture note, build and ctest invocations,
117:   manual remedy commands, mention of the clear configure error).
118: - `CHANGELOG.md`: under `[0.2.0-Unreleased]`, `### Fixed` bullet for the
119:   configure-time fixture/LFS check and `### Added` bullet for the README
120:   build/test instructions.
121: - CI workflow: unchanged; optional docs note only.

3: # TiffCraft
4: 
5: TiffCraft is a header-only C++ library for working with TIFF images. At the
6: moment, it requires C++20 or newer and contains functionality for reading TIFF
7: images in various uncompressed formats.
8: 
9: # Objectives
10: 
11: TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:
12: 
13: - Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
14: - C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
15: - Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
16: - Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
17:   - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
18:     on-going development.
19: 
20: # Usage
21: 
22: For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
23: word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
24: the following:
25: 
26: ```C++
27: #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
28: #include <functional>
29: 
30: int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
31:   if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
32:   TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
33:   TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter), loadParams);
34:   auto image = iffExporter.takeImage();
35: 
36:   // your own image processing code
37: 
38:   return 0;
39: }
40: ```
41: 
42: TiffExporterAny will decode and convert pixels to a flat-buffer (i.e.
43:  `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel
44: format. For example, an image with 2-bits per sample is exported as an 8-bit
45: image.
46: 
47: # Advanced usage
48: 
49: Users that prefer to decode and handle the image pixel data themselves, or need
50: to handle multiple frames per image, could write their own handler:
51:

53: #include <tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp>
54: #include <iostream>
55: 
56: int main() {
57:   TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
58:     [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
59:         const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
60:         TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
61:       std::cout << "Loaded IFD with " << ifd.entries().size()
62:                 << " entries." << std::endl;
63:       std::cout << "Image data size: " << imageData.size() << std::endl;
64: 
65:       // Add your own image processing code here
66: 
67:     });
68: 
69:   return 0;
70: }

7: images in various uncompressed formats.
8: 
9: # Objectives
10: 
11: TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:
12: 
13: - Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
14: - C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
15: - Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
16: - Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
17:   - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
18:     on-going development.
19: 
20: # Usage
21: 
22: For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
23: word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
24: the following:
25: 
26: ```C++
27: #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
28: #include <functional>
29: 
30: int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
31:   if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
32:   TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
33:   TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter), loadParams);
34:   auto image = iffExporter.takeImage();
35: 
36:   // your own image processing code
37: 
38:   return 0;
39: }
40: ```

43:  `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel

45: image.

54: #include <iostream>

+     "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libtiff-pics/*.tif2")

+endif()
+

+foreach(F IN LISTS PICS_TIFFS)
